Only layout, control sizing, and chrome differ. Breakpoint should follow whatever the app already uses; do not introduce a new one.\n\n***\n\n## Field order and behavior (both platforms)\n\n### 1. Title â€” primary field\n\n* First element in the body, autofocused on open.\n* Visually the largest input: \\~17px/600 on desktop, \\~18px/600 on mobile.\n* Placeholder `Card titleâ€¦`.\n* Required. Create is disabled (or shows an inline error) while empty. Trim before submit.\n\n### 2. Type â€” single-select pill row\n\n* Replaces the dropdown with one-click pills.\n* **Types are dynamic.** Render one pill per type from the app's existing type source (same source the board/card already uses). Do not hard-code type names, count, or order â€” the row must work for 2 types or 12.\n* **Colors are dynamic.** Each pill shows a small round dot (8px) filled with that type's own color, taken from the type record. Never hard-code hex values per type; if a type has no color, fall back to a neutral token (`--text-4`).\n* Selected state: tinted background + border in the app's primary token, primary text color. Unselected: subtle track background, secondary text, transparent border; hover raises contrast.\n* Default selection: the app's existing default type (first in the list if there is no configured default).\n* Overflow: desktop wraps to multiple lines; mobile scrolls horizontally in one row (no wrap, no visible scrollbar chrome).\n* Keyboard: arrow keys move between pills, Space/Enter selects; the row is a single tab stop (radiogroup semantics â€” `role=\"radiogroup\"` with `role=\"radio\"` + `aria-checked` children).\n\n### 3. Description â€” markdown text area, on-demand template\n\n* Labeled `Description`, with a quiet `Markdown` hint next to the label on desktop.\n* Monospace font at 13.5px, line-height \\~1.7, so it reads as editable source rather than rendered output.\n* Generously tall by default: \\~270px desktop, \\~260px mobile. Desktop is vertically resizable; mobile is not.\n* **Template is opt-in, not pre-filled.** A small `Template` button sits on the label row. Clicking inserts the markdown scaffold as plain editable text; the button then reads `Clear` and reverts the field. Rationale: most cards don't need all sections, and pre-filling forces deletion and makes an empty form look full.\n  * Only offer `Clear` while the body is still exactly the untouched template; once the user edits it, the button returns to `Template` and inserting again should append rather than overwrite. Never silently discard user-typed content.\n  * The template body itself should come from config, not be hard-coded in the component, so it can be edited later. (Optional follow-up, only if the team wants it: per-type templates keyed off the selected type â€” needs a template field on the type record, and switching type must not clobber edited text.)\n\n### 4. Target column â€” real control, not a label\n\n* Footer control reading `Add to <column>`, with the column's dot and name, opening the column list.\n* Defaults to the column the dialog was launched from.\n* The chosen column is what the card is created in.\n\n***\n\n## Platform specifics\n\n### Desktop dialog\n\n* \\~480px wide, auto height, on a dim scrim; card surface, 14px radius, elevated shadow, 1px border.\n* Header: small square primary-tinted icon tile with a plus glyph, title `New card`, spacer, icon-only close button on the right.\n* Footer bar (separated by a top border, page-background fill): column picker on the left, then `Cancel` (secondary) and `Create card` (primary) on the right.\n* **This is a Windows app** â€” the keyboard hint chip inside the primary button reads `Ctrl+â†µ`, not `âŒ˜â†µ`. Use Windows modifier labels everywhere.\n* Shortcuts: `Ctrl+Enter` submits from anywhere in the form (including the textarea); `Esc` cancels. If the form has unsaved content, `Esc` should confirm before discarding.\n* Button order follows the app's existing dialogs (`Run Dialog.dc.html`) â€” do not invent a new order for this one dialog.\n\n### Mobile sheet\n\n* Full-height sheet filling the viewport below the status bar; the body scrolls, header and footer are pinned.\n* Header: `Cancel` (left, secondary), `New card` (centered title), `Create` (right, primary-colored text). The top-bar Create and the footer button are the same action â€” keep them in sync for disabled state.\n* Pinned footer, two rows: the column picker row above a full-width `Create card` button. Two rows because the picker opens its own list and needs its own tappable row; side by side would squeeze both below a comfortable touch width.\n  * Acceptable alternative if a single-row footer is preferred: move the column picker up into the scrolling body as a normal field and pin only the Create button.\n* All touch targets â‰¥ 44px tall; type pills 40px.\n* Add safe-area bottom padding so the footer clears the home indicator.\n\n***\n\n## Visual system\n\n* Use only existing tokens from `STYLE_GUIDE.md` â€” surface, page, track, hover, border, border-strong, text-1â€¦4, primary, primary-strong, primary-bg, on-primary. No new colors.\n* Must render correctly in light and dark themes; verify pill selected/unselected contrast in both.\n* Focus rings: 1px primary border + 3px primary-tinted ring on every input and textarea, matching existing fields.\n* Radii: 8â€“9px desktop controls, 11â€“12px mobile controls, 14px dialog.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n* [ ] Opening the dialog focuses Title; the description is empty (no template text).\n* [ ] Type pills are generated from the dynamic type list with per-type colors from data; adding, removing, renaming, or recoloring a type is reflected with no code change.\n* [ ] Selecting a type is one click; selection is visible in both themes; keyboard-navigable as a radiogroup.\n* [ ] `Template` inserts editable markdown; `Clear` removes it; user edits are never lost without confirmation.\n* [ ] Description is at least \\~260px tall by default and monospace.\n* [ ] The target column can be changed in the dialog and the card is created in the chosen column.\n* [ ] `Ctrl+Enter` creates, `Esc` cancels (with confirm when dirty); no Mac modifier labels anywhere.\n* [ ] Create is disabled while Title is empty, on both platforms and in both mobile Create affordances.\n* [ ] Mobile: body scrolls, header/footer pinned, all targets â‰¥ 44px, footer clears the home indicator.\n\r\n\n===== design\\releases\\0_0_4\\F_91_remove_finished_reasoning_blocks.md =====\r\n---\nauthor: \nid: F_91\ninternalId: 3ffa4da3-1e0f-4930-ad38-6bf247b13c52\ntitle: remove finished reasoning blocks\nstatus: ready\nowner: \naffects:\nagents:\npolicy:\nafter: eb3a4820-0edb-4161-8fe5-926a981d2c8f\n---\n\nwhen a reasoning output of an agent finishes, we should remove the block\n\n## Current state\n\nCodex reasoning is stored as an `AgentConversationEvent`. Streaming updates replace the same event by `providerItemId`, changing its status from `inProgress` to `completed`. `ActionConversationChat` currently renders every reasoning event, so completed reasoning blocks remain visible during the live run and in reopened conversations. Failed and declined reasoning already use the error presentation.\n\n## implementation details\n\n- Filter conversation feed activities in `ActionConversationChat`: omit only events where `type === 'reasoning'` and `status === 'completed'`.\n- Keep in-progress, failed, declined and unknown-status reasoning visible.\n- Keep completed reasoning events in conversation data and persisted history; this is a presentation-only change.\n- Update chat tests for live completion, reopened conversations, failed/declined reasoning and unaffected non-reasoning activities.\n\n## acceptance criteria\n\n- In-progress reasoning is visible.\n- A reasoning block disappears when its status becomes `completed`, including after reopening a conversation.\n- Failed and declined reasoning remains visible with its error state and content.\n- Completed non-reasoning activities remain visible.\n\r\n\n===== design\\releases\\0_0_4\\F_94_no_prefill_prompt_running_conv.md =====\r\n---\nauthor: \nid: F_94\ninternalId: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\ntitle: no prefill prompt running conv\nstatus: ready\nowner: \naffects:\nagents:\npolicy:\nafter: 3ffa4da3-1e0f-4930-ad38-6bf247b13c52\n---\n\nWhen an agent is waiting for a response, but the action popup was closed or on the wrong 'action', then when the user clicks on the action to view the conversation and answer, the input box is prefilled again with the action's prompt. this is annoying cause it needs to be removed.\n\nso, when activating an action that has a running conversation, don't prefill the input\n\n# Current state\n\n`useActionPopupController` prepares an action's stored prompt for a new conversation. When popup opens on another action, or reopens while execution state is being restored, that prepared prompt can remain in `promptState` when user selects action with a `queued`, `running`, or `waitingForInput` conversation.\n\n# Implementation details\n\n- Give active execution its own prompt identity, including before active-child metadata arrives.\n- When active action is selected, seed editor only from its shared user-entered draft; otherwise show empty input.\n- Invalidate pending prompt preparation and bump `promptResetToken` when action becomes active.\n- Keep stored-prompt prefill for idle actions starting new conversations. Keep command actions unchanged.\n\n# Acceptance criteria\n\n- Selecting or reopening action with active conversation does not prefill its stored action prompt.\n- Existing user-entered draft for active conversation is restored.\n- Late prompt-preparation result cannot overwrite active conversation input.\n- Idle agent actions still prefill stored prompt.\n- Controller and popup tests cover action switching, popup reopen, draft restore, and preparation race.\n\r\n\n===== design\\releases\\0_0_4\\F_95_integrate_into_project_should_track_commit.md =====\r\n---\nauthor: \nid: F_95\ninternalId: e5b95f2c-cd0c-4623-8e12-d0c497447e71\ntitle: integrate into project should track commit\nstatus: ready\nowner: \naffects:\nagents:\n  - design/activity/card__e5b95f2c-cd0c-4623-8e12-d0c497447e71.json#conversation=agent-4e6f97b9-647e-49fc-93f7-cf09e5eff1aa\npolicy:\nafter: 9ef42f8e-d6f7-4514-8e4a-5555318c4b51\n---\n\n## Current state\n\n`WorktreeSelector` integrates an assigned card through `WorktreeService` and the Electron worktree service. The backend checkpoints primary-worktree changes, rebases the card branch when behind, then fast-forwards the project branch. The operation returns no commit metadata.\n\nCard commit history reads tracked `<projectFolder>/activity/card__<cardInternalId>.json` files. Only action executions add commit references, so commits integrated from the selector are absent unless an action already recorded them.\n\n## Implementation details\n\n- Add a card-specific integration request containing `cardInternalId` and `projectFolder`; project-level worktree integration remains untracked.\n- After any rebase, squash the card branch's complete change onto the project branch and create one integration commit. Do not fast-forward or retain the card branch's individual commits on the project branch.\n- Resolve the integration commit's activity metadata, then append one system activity record containing only that commit and labeled `Integrate into project` to the card's primary-checkout activity file. Do not model it as a user action.\n- Commit the activity-file update through the existing serialized activity writer. Return only after both integration and history persistence finish, so existing card-history reload and diff UI show the integration commit.\n- If applying or committing the squash fails, restore the primary checkout to its state after the primary-worktree checkpoint and before the squash attempt.\n- Failed integration writes no activity record. If integration succeeds but activity persistence fails, report that partial failure clearly; never claim tracking succeeded.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Integrating a card worktree with one or several outgoing commits creates and records exactly one squash commit under the card's stable `internalId`.\n- The squash commit contains the combined change between the project branch and the rebased card branch. Primary checkpoint and activity-file commits are not included.\n- The squash commit appears once under `Integrate into project` in the existing card commit selector and opens one combined diff for the integration.\n- Integration with no outgoing commits or no combined change remains rejected and creates no activity record.\n- Failed integration creates no activity record. History-persistence failure after a successful squash commit is visible.\n- Project-level worktree integration creates no card activity.\n- Tests cover one and several source commits producing one squash commit, rebase before integration, stable card ownership, squash cleanup and persistence failure paths, and project-level exclusion.\n\r\n\n===== design\\releases\\0_0_4\\F_96_ctrl_enter_on_action_input.md =====\r\n---\nauthor: \nid: F_96\ninternalId: d33002d3-ee0e-4c08-8e26-36f790500ee2\ntitle: ctrl enter on action input\nstatus: ready\nowner: \naffects:\nagents:\npolicy:\nafter: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\n---\n\nwhen pressing ctrl + enter on action input, the input is sent, this is good, but before this happens, the input box still adds an enter, which should not be the case.\n\n# Current state\n\n`ActionAgentPrompt` handles `Ctrl+Enter` and `Meta+Enter` on the prompt wrapper during event bubbling. MDXEditor handles `Enter` first, inserts a newline, then the wrapper flushes and sends the changed prompt.\n\n# Implementation details\n\n- Intercept `Ctrl+Enter` and `Meta+Enter` during capture, before MDXEditor handles the key.\n- Prevent default behavior and stop propagation, then flush the latest prompt before running the existing shortcut callback.\n- Keep plain `Enter`, `Shift+Enter`, and disabled shortcut behavior unchanged.\n- Extend `action_agent_prompt.test.tsx` with regression coverage proving the editor does not receive the send shortcut.\n\n# Acceptance criteria\n\n- `Ctrl+Enter` sends current prompt without inserting a newline.\n- `Meta+Enter` has same behavior.\n- Prompt is flushed before send callback runs.\n- Plain `Enter` and `Shift+Enter` still insert newlines.\n\r\n",

Do not fast-forward or retain the card branch's individual commits on the project branch.\n- Resolve the integration commit's activity metadata, then append one system activity record containing only that commit and labeled `Integrate into project` to the card's primary-checkout activity file. Do not model it as a user action.\n- Commit the activity-file update through the existing serialized activity writer. Return only after both integration and history persistence finish, so existing card-history reload and diff UI show the integration commit.\n- If applying or committing the squash fails, restore the primary checkout to its state after the primary-worktree checkpoint and before the squash attempt.\n- Failed integration writes no activity record. If integration succeeds but activity persistence fails, report that partial failure clearly; never claim tracking succeeded.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Integrating a card worktree with one or several outgoing commits creates and records exactly one squash commit under the card's stable `internalId`.\n- The squash commit contains the combined change between the project branch and the rebased card branch. Primary checkpoint and activity-file commits are not included.\n- The squash commit appears once under `Integrate into project` in the existing card commit selector and opens one combined diff for the integration.\n- Integration with no outgoing commits or no combined change remains rejected and creates no activity record.\n- Failed integration creates no activity record. History-persistence failure after a successful squash commit is visible.\n- Project-level worktree integration creates no card activity.\n- Tests cover one and several source commits producing one squash commit, rebase before integration, stable card ownership, squash cleanup and persistence failure paths, and project-level exclusion.\n\r\n\n===== design\\releases\\0_0_4\\F_96_ctrl_enter_on_action_input.md =====\r\n---\nauthor: \nid: F_96\ninternalId: d33002d3-ee0e-4c08-8e26-36f790500ee2\ntitle: ctrl enter on action input\nstatus: ready\nowner: \naffects:\nagents:\npolicy:\nafter: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\n---\n\nwhen pressing ctrl + enter on action input, the input is sent, this is good, but before this happens, the input box still adds an enter, which should not be the case.\n\n# Current state\n\n`ActionAgentPrompt` handles `Ctrl+Enter` and `Meta+Enter` on the prompt wrapper during event bubbling. MDXEditor handles `Enter` first, inserts a newline, then the wrapper flushes and sends the changed prompt.\n\n# Implementation details\n\n- Intercept `Ctrl+Enter` and `Meta+Enter` during capture, before MDXEditor handles the key.\n- Prevent default behavior and stop propagation, then flush the latest prompt before running the existing shortcut callback.\n- Keep plain `Enter`, `Shift+Enter`, and disabled shortcut behavior unchanged.\n- Extend `action_agent_prompt.test.tsx` with regression coverage proving the editor does not receive the send shortcut.\n\n# Acceptance criteria\n\n- `Ctrl+Enter` sends current prompt without inserting a newline.\n- `Meta+Enter` has same behavior.\n- Prompt is flushed before send callback runs.\n- Plain `Enter` and `Shift+Enter` still insert newlines.\n\r\n",

Deletion flushes pending commits, repairs the following card's `after` link when needed, deletes the file, applies push mode, then calls `reloadCurrentProjectSnapshot`. That reload reads every project file and the repository index, rebuilds all cards, ensures internal IDs, and reloads agent conversations.\n\n## implementation details\n\n- After storage deletion succeeds, update `ProjectState` directly: merge the committed ordering-repair file, remove the deleted path from loaded files and `repositoryFiles`, and rebuild the snapshot once.\n- Dispatch existing data-service change and card events so board, file tree, open documents, and selection react normally.\n- Remove `reloadCurrentProjectSnapshot` from the shared file-deletion path; keep full reloads for operations that cannot derive their local result.\n- Preserve pending-commit flushing, ordering repair, SHA use, auto/manual push behavior, and unchanged local state when deletion fails.\n- Update `card_operations` regression tests to prove deletion performs no full project or repository-index reload.\n\n## acceptance criteria\n\n- Deleting a card removes it from the board, file tree, loaded files, and repository index without calling `reloadCurrentProjectSnapshot`, `loadProject`, or `listRepositoryFiles`.\n- A deleted middle card's follower has the correct persisted and in-memory `after` value.\n- Existing card removal/change events close or refresh affected views without reloading agent conversations.\n- Failed deletion leaves the local snapshot unchanged; pending-save and push-mode behavior remains unchanged.\n- Card deletion and file-tree deletion tests pass.\n\r\n\n===== B_86_scroll_on_cardview.md =====\r\n---\nauthor: \nid: B_86\ninternalId: fb78171f-6c8d-4760-8e63-7ac2eff93256\ntitle: Scroll on cardview\nstatus: ready\nowner: \naffects:\nagents:\n  - design/activity/card__fb78171f-6c8d-4760-8e63-7ac2eff93256.json#conversation=agent-97ea4269-4ceb-4668-996c-394ef6c17461\n  - design/activity/card__fb78171f-6c8d-4760-8e63-7ac2eff93256.json#conversation=agent-a957a84b-06b9-401d-a353-05e3a23df0c2\n  - design/activity/card__fb78171f-6c8d-4760-8e63-7ac2eff93256.json#conversation=agent-1b4980cc-b005-4bfd-b788-67647496320e\npolicy:\nafter: 0f5a1edf-4b4e-4dea-8c7a-05df83ae1288\n---\n\nOn mobile, cards view does not scroll. We should already have made a component for this.\n\n## Current state\n\n- `CardView` renders `CardViewScrollZones` on mobile and scrolls its card-columns container from pointer movement at either edge.\n- Each transparent zone is only 3 px wide. This is too narrow for reliable touch input, while card surfaces suppress native scrolling for drag-and-drop.\n- Existing tests invoke the zones directly and therefore do not expose the unusable touch target.\n\n## implementation details\n\n- Keep `CardViewScrollZones`; widen both zones to the 20 px mobile card-view gutters using one named constant.\n- Keep zones above card drag surfaces and preserve existing pointer capture, scroll direction, cancellation, native scroll boundaries, card dragging, and desktop behavior.\n- Verify the regression on a mobile viewport. Keep existing interaction tests; do not add a test tied only to the visual width constant.\n\n## acceptance criteria\n\n- On mobile, dragging vertically from either outer card-view gutter reliably scrolls the card columns when cards fill the viewport.\n- Edge gestures do not drag, open, or activate cards and stop on pointer up or cancellation.\n- Card interaction outside the edge zones and desktop card-view behavior remain unchanged.\n\r\n\n===== B_87_card_changed_not_pushed_to_mobile.md =====\r\n---\nauthor: \nid: B_87\ninternalId: 1b39ee56-e06e-4705-840f-7541b2a57d3d\ntitle: Card changed not pushed to mobile\nstatus: ready\nowner: \naffects:\nagents:\n  - design/activity/card__1b39ee56-e06e-4705-840f-7541b2a57d3d.json#conversation=agent-6e7b30ea-5d5c-439b-b2b0-7f656fe5a400\n  - design/activity/card__1b39ee56-e06e-4705-840f-7541b2a57d3d.json#conversation=agent-c6f98940-00b7-4041-a50e-fe0c85838b84\npolicy:\nafter: b692b422-3e30-4518-91c1-bcee5451b046\n---\n\nWhen an agent changes a card and the app is running in electron, the app gets updates and the card refreshed. This does not happen when app is on mobile and connected to electron.\n\nWe should verify if every message type is correctly implemented over websockets\n\n## Current state\n\nElectron's project watcher emits card changes through `watchProject`. Remote-control server forwards them as WebSocket `watchProject` events, and `RemoteControlStorageService` invokes registered callback. `ProjectLoading` then tries to reload changed markdown file, but stops because remote storage does not implement optional `loadFile`. Card therefore stays stale on mobile. Desktop storage implements `loadFile` through same dispatcher.\n\n## implementation details\n\n- Add `RemoteControlStorageService.loadFile` and proxy it through existing WebSocket request protocol. Server dispatcher already exposes method.\n- Keep existing `watchProject` event and project reload flow; no separate card-change message needed.\n- Add regression coverage for watch event followed by remote file load and refreshed project state.\n- Audit all server-push message names and payloads against client handlers: `watchProject`, `agentRun`, `actionRun`, `codexRateLimits`, and `worktreesChanged`. Cover subscription setup and cleanup.\n\n## acceptance criteria\n\n- Agent change to card file appears on connected mobile app without reopening project.\n- Added, changed, and removed markdown files received through `watchProject` update mobile project state.\n- Remote `loadFile` returns same markdown payload and errors as Electron bridge.\n- Every server-push message type has matching client handling and round-trip test coverage.\n- Existing Electron project watching remains unchanged.\n\r\n\n===== F_100_when_waiting_for_input_timer_should_stop.md =====\r\n---\nauthor: \nid: F_100\ninternalId: b692b422-3e30-4518-91c1-bcee5451b046\ntitle: when waiting for input timer should stop\nstatus: ready\nowner: \naffects:\nagents:\n  - design/activity/card__b692b422-3e30-4518-91c1-bcee5451b046.json#conversation=agent-332f2b3e-fd65-4d76-ad55-c2d70f1b9b25\n  - design/activity/card__b692b422-3e30-4518-91c1-bcee5451b046.json#conversation=agent-920bd107-7631-4ebb-9c0b-31d6db64d8db\npolicy:\nafter: fb78171f-6c8d-4760-8e63-7ac2eff93256\n---\n\non the action popup, when the state is 'waiting for input', the timer should stop counting and only restart again once the input has been provided.\n\n# Current state\n\n`ConversationTimer` receives only `startedAt` and `completedAt`. While `completedAt` is null, it updates every second regardless of action status, so time spent in `waitingForInput` is counted.\n\n`ActionConversationChat` already receives canonical run status and renders timer, but does not pass status to it.\n\n# Implementation details\n\n- Pass run status from `ActionConversationChat` to `ConversationTimer`.\n- Keep elapsed value in timer and update it only while status is running.\n- On `waitingForInput`, freeze current value and stop interval. On `running`, resume from frozen value.\n- Keep completed and uninterrupted-run behavior unchanged. Do not add persistence or backend timing fields.\n- Add timer tests for running, waiting, resumed, and completed states.\n\n# Acceptance criteria\n\n- Timer stops changing while run status is `waitingForInput`.\n- Providing input changes status to `running`; timer continues from frozen value without counting waiting time.\n- Timer remains static after completion.\n- Runs that never wait keep current timer behavior.\n\r\n\n===== F_109_add_access_level_option_for_agents.md =====\r\n---\nauthor: \nid: F_109\ninternalId: 0f5a1edf-4b4e-4dea-8c7a-05df83ae1288\ntitle: add access-level option for agents\nstatus: ready\nowner: \naffects:\nagents:\n  - design/activity/card__0f5a1edf-4b4e-4dea-8c7a-05df83ae1288.json#conversation=agent-61257114-41c8-4311-a5e7-8d8d4e79471d\npolicy:\nafter: 0b35236a-2fe4-4b58-86f8-bd84af5ac7ce\n---\n## Current state\n\nMDÂ² selects agent, model, and thinking level globally, per action, and per run. Agent profiles define model choices and command arguments. Access level and approval policy are not represented in profiles, action definitions, run requests, or UI controls.\n\nAgent commands therefore omit both settings. Codex and Claude use provider defaults or user configuration, so MDÂ² cannot show, validate, or audit effective permissions.\n\n## Implementation details\n\n- Add provider-specific access-level and approval-policy choices, argument names, and defaults to each agent profile. Keep provider wording unchanged; built-in Codex choices use `read-only`, `workspace-write`, and `danger-full-access`, plus `untrusted`, `on-request`, and `never`.\n- Add `desktop.accessLevel` and `desktop.approvalPolicy` defaults. Add optional `accessLevel` and `approvalPolicy` overrides to agent action definitions and run input. Resolution order is run override, action override, then desktop default.\n- Show profile-supported choices beside agent, model, and thinking level in config, action editor, and local run/chat controls. Changing agent resets incompatible selections to that profile's defaults. Clearly report profiles that do not expose either capability.\n- Validate profile definitions, saved actions, renderer requests, and Electron execution. Reject unknown values, missing argument mappings, or values unsupported by selected agent before process start.\n- Add resolved arguments before one-shot, resume, and streaming subcommands. For built-in Codex, use `--sandbox <accessLevel>` and `--ask-for-approval <approvalPolicy>`; other profiles use their configured arguments without MDÂ² translating provider terms.\n- Propagate effective values through scheduled, chained, continued, local-bridge, and remote-control runs. Record them in execution events and action history.\n- Add profile, config persistence, action validation/editor, popup/controller, request-contract, command-building, execution, bridge, remote-control, continuation, and scheduling tests.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Each agent exposes only its configured access levels and approval policies, using provider-specific names.\n- User can set global defaults, action overrides, and local run/chat overrides for both settings.\n- Run override wins over action override; action override wins over desktop default.\n- Codex receives exact resolved `--sandbox` and `--ask-for-approval` values for one-shot, resumed, and streaming runs.\n- Unsupported, stale, or malformed selections fail before process start with a clear error.\n- Switching agents cannot retain incompatible access or approval selections.\n- Scheduled, chained, continued, local, and remote runs use and report effective settings consistently.\n- Existing agent/model/thinking-level behavior, approval handling, and execution tests remain valid.\n\r\n\n===== F_111_remove_new_conv_led_upon_load_conv.md =====\r\n---\nauthor: \nid: F_111\ninternalId: 6fdba724-f0ab-484a-9831-0480bc6d5e8d\ntitle: remove new conv-led upon load conv\nstatus: ready\nowner: \naffects:\nagents:\n  - design/activity/card__6fdba724-f0ab-484a-9831-0480bc6d5e8d.json#conversation=agent-f72013d8-6964-4773-8e15-c3efcc2c41f0\npolicy:\nafter: 1b39ee56-e06e-4705-840f-7541b2a57d3d\n---\nWhen an agent is finished, we show a small blue led on the 'action' button in the `action-popup`. This is ok. However, it remains there for as long as the action popup remains open. Also, the user initially gets to see an empty chat window, which is confusing. So:\n\n* when an action completes while the chatlog of that action is active (so action-popup open and action button selected), then we should mark the log as `viewed`\n* when the user clicks on an action button that has a log still marked as `ready but not yet viewed`, then instead of showing an empty log history, immediately open the last log (that is marked as ready, not yet viewed).\n* as soon as the log is shown, remove the led from the action button. the log has been viewed, so lets show it this way.\n\n## Current state\n\n`agentAcknowledgementService` stores one completed-result checkpoint per card. `CardRunButton` derives unseen action IDs when opening a popup, and `CardActionPopupService` keeps that copied list for popup lifetime. `ActionConversationChat` acknowledges a completed conversation once rendered, but copied selector state does not update, so blue LED remains.\n\n`useActionPopupController` automatically restores latest waiting conversation only. Selecting action with unseen completed result therefore starts with empty chat until user selects history manually.\n\n## implementation details\n\n- Derive latest unseen completed conversation per action from current card conversations and acknowledgement checkpoint. Keep popup data reactive while open; remove frozen unseen-ID snapshot. Preserve existing local-storage format and card-level checkpoint semantics.\n- When user selects action with unseen results, load newest unseen conversation. Keep normal empty-conversation state for actions without unseen results and for explicit `Conversations` reset.\n- Acknowledge only after completed conversation is displayed. This covers action completing while selected and removes both action LED and card unseen indicator immediately.\n- Keep result unseen if conversation load fails and report existing load error.\n- Add acknowledgement-query, popup-selection, active-completion, multiple-result, and load-failure regression tests.\n\n## acceptance criteria\n\n- Clicking action with unseen results immediately shows newest unseen conversation; empty chat is not shown first.\n- Showing conversation clears action LED and card unseen-result indicator without closing popup.\n- Action completing while its chat is selected is marked viewed and leaves no LED.\n- Action completing while another action is selected remains marked unseen until opened.\n- Multiple unseen results open newest result; existing checkpoint marks it and older results viewed.\n- Failed load leaves result unseen and shows error.\n\r\n",

Keep provider wording unchanged; built-in Codex choices use `read-only`, `workspace-write`, and `danger-full-access`, plus `untrusted`, `on-request`, and `never`.\n- Add `desktop.accessLevel` and `desktop.approvalPolicy` defaults. Record them in execution events and action history.\n- Add profile, config persistence, action validation/editor, popup/controller, request-contract, command-building, execution, bridge, remote-control, continuation, and scheduling tests.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- Each agent exposes only its configured access levels and approval policies, using provider-specific names.\n- User can set global defaults, action overrides, and local run/chat overrides for both settings.\n- Run override wins over action override; action override wins over desktop default.\n- Codex receives exact resolved `--sandbox` and `--ask-for-approval` values for one-shot, resumed, and streaming runs.\n- Unsupported, stale, or malformed selections fail before process start with a clear error.\n- Switching agents cannot retain incompatible access or approval selections.\n- Scheduled, chained, continued, local, and remote runs use and report effective settings consistently.\n- Existing agent/model/thinking-level behavior, approval handling, and execution tests remain valid.\n\r\n\n===== F_111_remove_new_conv_led_upon_load_conv.md =====\r\n---\nauthor: \nid: F_111\ninternalId: 6fdba724-f0ab-484a-9831-0480bc6d5e8d\ntitle: remove new conv-led upon load conv\nstatus: ready\nowner: \naffects:\nagents:\n  - design/activity/card__6fdba724-f0ab-484a-9831-0480bc6d5e8d.json#conversation=agent-f72013d8-6964-4773-8e15-c3efcc2c41f0\npolicy:\nafter: 1b39ee56-e06e-4705-840f-7541b2a57d3d\n---\nWhen an agent is finished, we show a small blue led on the 'action' button in the `action-popup`. Selecting action with unseen completed result therefore starts with empty chat until user selects history manually.\n\n## implementation details\n\n- Derive latest unseen completed conversation per action from current card conversations and acknowledgement checkpoint. The processes appear as **Git for Windows** in Task Manager and accumulate across runs.\\r\\n\\r\\nObserved processes were executing normally short-lived commands such as `config`, `rev-parse`, `remote -v`, and `status --porcelain`. They remained alive after their immediate parent processes had exited.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current implementation\\r\\n\\r\\nMDÂ² starts agents through `AgentRunnerService`. When an agent closes normally, `handleClose` queries the current Windows process tree and terminates descendants of the agent PID. Cancellation terminates the process tree with `taskkill /t /f`.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis cleanup cannot discover a surviving Git process after an intermediate parent has already exited: the current process snapshot no longer contains a complete chain from the agent PID to that Git process. The observed Git processes had dead immediate parents, matching this failure mode.\\r\\n\\r\\nMDÂ² also invokes Git directly through `git_commands.js`. These calls have no timeout or cancellation handling, so an independently hung app-owned Git command can block its caller indefinitely.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Investigation plan\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Reproduce with MDÂ² open but no agent run, then while starting and completing or cancelling an agent run.\\r\\n2. Record every spawned Git PID, command, working directory, parent PID, agent run ID, and lifecycle event.\\r\\n3. Run an affected command under a bounded external timeout with Git tracing enabled to locate the blocking operation.\\r\\n4. Check repository state, Git configuration, filesystem monitoring, antivirus or file locks, and agent shutdown ordering.\\r\\n5. Confirm whether Git descendants become disconnected before `AgentRunnerService.handleClose` takes its process snapshot.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required change\\r\\n\\r\\n- Track enough process ownership during an agent run to terminate surviving descendants even when intermediate processes exit before final cleanup.\\r\\n- Clean up owned descendants when an agent completes, fails, is cancelled, or crashes.\\r\\n- Do not terminate unrelated Git processes or Git work started outside the corresponding MDÂ² agent run.\\r\\n- Add a bounded timeout and process cleanup to direct Git execution in `git_commands.js`.\\r\\n- Include the command, working directory, elapsed time, and owning run or app operation in timeout diagnostics.\\r\\n- Deduplicate or serialize repeated read-only metadata probes only if tracing confirms they contribute to the accumulation.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Failure modes and compatibility\\r\\n\\r\\n- PID reuse must not allow cleanup to target a process that MDÂ² did not start.\\r\\n- Cleanup must cover shell and helper-process chains used by Git for Windows on Windows.\\r\\n- Long-running network Git operations need an explicit, suitable timeout rather than the same threshold as local metadata commands.\\r\\n- Existing agent cancellation, command actions, commits, worktree operations, push, pull, and fetch behavior must remain unchanged apart from bounded failure and cleanup.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] Completing, failing, cancelling, or crashing an agent run leaves no Git processes owned by that run.\\r\\n- [ ] Repeated agent runs do not accumulate Git for Windows processes.\\r\\n\\n===== B_85_add_the_reference_to_a_chatlog_to_a_card_as_soon_as_possible.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: B_85\\r\\ninternalId: 56dd54b0-9554-4545-85d4-bb45efef4d6e\\r\\ntitle: add the reference to a chatlog to a card as soon as possible\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\n  - Failed and declined reasoning already use the error presentation.\\r\\n\\r\\n## implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Filter conversation feed activities in `ActionConversationChat`: omit only events where `type === 'reasoning'` and `status === 'completed'`.\\r\\n- Keep in-progress, failed, declined and unknown-status reasoning visible.\\r\\n- Keep completed reasoning events in conversation data and persisted history; this is a presentation-only change.\\r\\n- Update chat tests for live completion, reopened conversations, failed/declined reasoning and unaffected non-reasoning activities.\\r\\n\\r\\n## acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- In-progress reasoning is visible.\\r\\n- A reasoning block disappears when its status becomes `completed`, including after reopening a conversation.\\r\\n- Failed and declined reasoning remains visible with its error state and content.\\r\\n- Completed non-reasoning activities remain visible.\\r\\n\\n===== F_94_no_prefill_prompt_running_conv.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_94\\r\\ninternalId: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\\r\\ntitle: no prefill prompt running conv\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 3ffa4da3-1e0f-4930-ad38-6bf247b13c52\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen an agent is waiting for a response, but the action popup was closed or on the wrong 'action', then when the user clicks on the action to view the conversation and answer, the input box is prefilled again with the action's prompt. this is annoying cause it needs to be removed.\\r\\n\\r\\nso, when activating an action that has a running conversation, don't prefill the input\\r\\n\\r\\n# Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`useActionPopupController` prepares an action's stored prompt for a new conversation. When popup opens on another action, or reopens while execution state is being restored, that prepared prompt can remain in `promptState` when user selects action with a `queued`, `running`, or `waitingForInput` conversation.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Give active execution its own prompt identity, including before active-child metadata arrives.\\r\\n- When active action is selected, seed editor only from its shared user-entered draft; otherwise show empty input.\\r\\n- Invalidate pending prompt preparation and bump `promptResetToken` when action becomes active.\\r\\n- Keep stored-prompt prefill for idle actions starting new conversations. Keep command actions unchanged.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Selecting or reopening action with active conversation does not prefill its stored action prompt.\\r\\n- Existing user-entered draft for active conversation is restored.\\r\\n- Late prompt-preparation result cannot overwrite active conversation input.\\r\\n- Idle agent actions still prefill stored prompt.\\r\\n- Controller and popup tests cover action switching, popup reopen, draft restore, and preparation race.\\r\\n\\n===== F_95_integrate_into_project_should_track_commit.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_95\\r\\ninternalId: e5b95f2c-cd0c-4623-8e12-d0c497447e71\\r\\ntitle: integrate into project should track commit\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\n  - design/activity/card__e5b95f2c-cd0c-4623-8e12-d0c497447e71.json#conversation=agent-4e6f97b9-647e-49fc-93f7-cf09e5eff1aa\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 9ef42f8e-d6f7-4514-8e4a-5555318c4b51\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`WorktreeSelector` integrates an assigned card through `WorktreeService` and the Electron worktree service. The backend checkpoints primary-worktree changes, rebases the card branch when behind, then fast-forwards the project branch. The operation returns no commit metadata.\\r\\n\\r\\nCard commit history reads tracked `<projectFolder>/activity/card__<cardInternalId>.json` files. Only action executions add commit references, so commits integrated from the selector are absent unless an action already recorded them.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Add a card-specific integration request containing `cardInternalId` and `projectFolder`; project-level worktree integration remains untracked.\\r\\n- After any rebase, squash the card branch's complete change onto the project branch and create one integration commit. Do not model it as a user action.\\r\\n- Commit the activity-file update through the existing serialized activity writer. Return only after both integration and history persistence finish, so existing card-history reload and diff UI show the integration commit.\\r\\n- If applying or committing the squash fails, restore the primary checkout to its state after the primary-worktree checkpoint and before the squash attempt.\\r\\n- Failed integration writes no activity record. If integration succeeds but activity persistence fails, report that partial failure clearly; never claim tracking succeeded.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Integrating a card worktree with one or several outgoing commits creates and records exactly one squash commit under the card's stable `internalId`.\\r\\n- The squash commit contains the combined change between the project branch and the rebased card branch. Primary checkpoint and activity-file commits are not included.\\r\\n- The squash commit appears once under `Integrate into project` in the existing card commit selector and opens one combined diff for the integration.\\r\\n- Integration with no outgoing commits or no combined change remains rejected and creates no activity record.\\r\\n- Failed integration creates no activity record. History-persistence failure after a successful squash commit is visible.\\r\\n- Project-level worktree integration creates no card activity.\\r\\n- Tests cover one and several source commits producing one squash commit, rebase before integration, stable card ownership, squash cleanup and persistence failure paths, and project-level exclusion.\\r\\n\\n===== F_96_ctrl_enter_on_action_input.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_96\\r\\ninternalId: d33002d3-ee0e-4c08-8e26-36f790500ee2\\r\\ntitle: ctrl enter on action input\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nwhen pressing ctrl + enter on action input, the input is sent, this is good, but before this happens, the input box still adds an enter, which should not be the case.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`ActionAgentPrompt` handles `Ctrl+Enter` and `Meta+Enter` on the prompt wrapper during event bubbling. MDXEditor handles `Enter` first, inserts a newline, then the wrapper flushes and sends the changed prompt.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Intercept `Ctrl+Enter` and `Meta+Enter` during capture, before MDXEditor handles the key.\\r\\n- Prevent default behavior and stop propagation, then flush the latest prompt before running the existing shortcut callback.\\r\\n- Keep plain `Enter`, `Shift+Enter`, and disabled shortcut behavior unchanged.\\r\\n- Extend `action_agent_prompt.test.tsx` with regression coverage proving the editor does not receive the send shortcut.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- `Ctrl+Enter` sends current prompt without inserting a newline.\\r\\n- `Meta+Enter` has same behavior.\\r\\n- Prompt is flushed before send callback runs.\\r\\n- Plain `Enter` and `Shift+Enter` still insert newlines.\\r\\n\\n===== F_98_worktree_vs_project_folder_placeholders.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_98\\r\\ninternalId: ff356504-eed4-47f3-bb38-2c749b6fcba6\\r\\ntitle: worktree vs project folder placeholders\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: d33002d3-ee0e-4c08-8e26-36f790500ee2\\r\\n---\\r\\nWe have 'rootProjectFolder' placeholder. this currently maps to the folder that the agent is running on, so it could the the main project folder or a worktree. \\r\\n\\r\\nWe need to improve this and split it up in `worktree-folder` and 'project-folder' where the last one always references the main project folder while 'worktree-folder' references the folder that the agent is currently running in.\\r\\n\\r\\nAlso, we need to add the 'releases-folder' as well\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n- `{{rootProjectFolder}}` exists in action prompt/command and diff-command placeholder sets.\\r\\n- Action execution resolves it to the execution checkout, which may be the opened project folder or a linked worktree. Diff commands resolve it to the opened project folder.\\r\\n- Action editor insertion controls and user documentation expose only the existing placeholder.\\r\\n\\r\\n## implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Replace `{{rootProjectFolder}}` everywhere with `{{worktree-folder}}` and `{{project-folder}}`; do not keep a legacy alias.\\r\\n- `{{worktree-folder}}` resolves to the absolute execution checkout path. When no linked worktree is selected, it equals `{{project-folder}}`.\\r\\n- `{{project-folder}}` always resolves to the absolute opened repository path, including during linked-worktree execution.\\r\\n- Add `{{releases-folder}}`, resolving to the configured repository-relative releases path: `<projectFolder>/<releasesFolder>`.\\r\\n- Support all three placeholders in action prompts, action commands, prompt preparation, diff commands, editor insertion controls, validation, and documentation.\\r\\n- Fail before process start when a required placeholder value is unavailable. Add tests for primary and linked-worktree execution, custom release paths, diff commands, insertion controls, and removed `{{rootProjectFolder}}` support.\\r\\n\\r\\n## acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Primary-checkout actions resolve `{{worktree-folder}}` and `{{project-folder}}` to the opened repository path.\\r\\n- Linked-worktree actions resolve `{{worktree-folder}}` to that worktree and `{{project-folder}}` to the opened repository path.\\r\\n- `{{releases-folder}}` returns the configured path relative to repository root, independent of active checkout.\\r\\n- Action prompts, action commands, and diff commands use the same three folder placeholders.\\r\\n- Editors and documentation list the new placeholders and no longer list `{{rootProjectFolder}}`.\\r\\n- `{{rootProjectFolder}}` is not resolved.\\r\\n\\n===== J_020_unify_agent_conversation_entries.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-020\\r\\ninternalId: 4edefccb-f7e3-4ae1-9c0d-5939ac1d3745\\r\\ntitle: unify agent conversation messages and events into ordered entries\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n  - shared/agent_conversations.mjs\\r\\n  - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_conversation.js\\r\\n  - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_runner_service.js\\r\\n  - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_transcript.js\\r\\n  - app/src/data/data_types.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/data/action_run_types.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/services/actions/action_execution_service.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/services/agents/card_agent_state.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/use_action_popup_controller.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/action_conversation_chat.tsx\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n  checkLinting: true\\r\\n  requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: c5d963f2-ca43-419d-bc3c-972199b7e7cd\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nReplace the parallel agent-conversation `messages` and `events` arrays with one canonical ordered `entries` array. Array position is ingestion order and is the only display order.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis refactor must land before the action-popup rendering-isolation work. That work must consume the single entry list and must not preserve the current merge-and-sort path.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Terminology\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Conversation entry**: one ordered item in an agent conversation.\\r\\n- **Message entry**: user or assistant text.\\r\\n- **Event entry**: reasoning, tool use, command execution, diagnostics, failures, and lifecycle observations.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not use **activity** for a conversation entry, field, helper, component, or collection. `activity` remains valid only for the separate card/project activity-storage domain.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current architecture\\r\\n\\r\\nPersisted `AgentConversation` stores `messages` and `events` separately. Live execution repeats the split as `LiveAgentTurn.messages` and `LiveAgentTurn.activities`. Producers append or replace items in those separate collections, while chat and transcript consumers merge and sort them by `sequence` to reconstruct ingestion order.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe split causes:\\r\\n\\r\\n- duplicate persisted and live representations;\\r\\n- inconsistent `event`/`activity` terminology;\\r\\n- repeated merge and sort work in consumers;\\r\\n- a rebuilt full `AgentConversation` projection in the popup controller;\\r\\n- ordering behavior owned by presentation code instead of the producer.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required model\\r\\n\\r\\nUse a discriminated union and one collection:\\r\\n\\r\\n```ts\\r\\n\\n===== J_021_derive_markdown_styles_globally.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-021\\r\\ninternalId: 11ffc4ac-44e0-4dab-a8d9-af9e83a43aff\\r\\ntitle: derive active Markdown content styles once in the global theme\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n  - app/src/theme/theme_context.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/theme/theme_provider.tsx\\r\\n  - app/src/theme/theme_provider.test.tsx\\r\\n  - app/src/theme/use_app_theme.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/components/editor/markdown_style_sx.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/components/editor/markdown_editor.tsx\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/action_conversation_chat.tsx\\r\\n  - app/src/components/config/markdown_style_preview.tsx\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n  checkLinting: true\\r\\n  requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: 4edefccb-f7e3-4ae1-9c0d-5939ac1d3745\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nBuild the active Markdown content styling once when the global Markdown style configuration changes. Components that render active Markdown consume the stable derived style and never rebuild it during unrelated renders.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis job is independent of the action-popup subscription refactor and should land before performance verification of that refactor.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current architecture\\r\\n\\r\\n`AppThemeProvider` owns `markdownStyleConfig`, but consumers receive only the raw configuration. Both `MarkdownEditor` and `ActionConversationChat` call `buildMarkdownContentSx(markdownStyleConfig)` in their render bodies. The builder creates a new nested MUI style object even when the configuration is unchanged.\\r\\n\\r\\n`MarkdownStylePreview` also calls the builder, but it renders an explicit configuration draft rather than the active global style.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required change\\r\\n\\r\\n- Derive a stable `markdownContentSx` value in `AppThemeProvider` with `useMemo`, depending only on `markdownStyleConfig`.\\r\\n- Expose the derived value through `AppThemeContextValue` and its fallback value.\\r\\n- Make `MarkdownEditor` and `ActionConversationChat` consume `markdownContentSx` directly.\\r\\n- Do not call `buildMarkdownContentSx` from either component.\\r\\n- Keep `buildMarkdownContentSx` as a pure derivation function owned by the theme/style layer.\\r\\n- Memoize `MarkdownStylePreview`'s derived style by its explicit `config` prop. The preview cannot consume the active global style because it must show unsaved draft configuration.\\r\\n- Do not introduce a service class; this is a pure derived theme value.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Identity contract\\r\\n\\r\\n- `markdownContentSx` retains object identity across renders when `markdownStyleConfig` is unchanged.\\r\\n- Changing palette mode, popup state, editor content, conversation content, or unrelated configuration does not rebuild it.\\r\\n- Changing the active Markdown style configuration rebuilds it once and updates all active Markdown consumers.\\r\\n- Changing the preview's explicit draft configuration rebuilds only the preview value.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Testing implications\\r\\n\\r\\n- Theme-provider tests prove the derived style is exposed and retains identity across unrelated provider renders.\\r\\n- Theme-provider tests prove changing `markdownStyleConfig` replaces the derived value.\\r\\n\\n===== J_022_stabilize_action_prompt_drafts.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-022\\r\\ninternalId: 5b39ff1e-4bbc-4d50-b527-36e1d1faa6f5\\r\\ntitle: move action prompt drafts out of popup React state\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/action_prompt_draft.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/action_agent_prompt.tsx\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/action_popup_bottom_row.tsx\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/action_popup_content.tsx\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/use_action_popup_controller.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/services/actions/action_execution_service.ts\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n  checkLinting: true\\r\\n  requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: 11ffc4ac-44e0-4dab-a8d9-af9e83a43aff\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nGive each action prompt draft one lifetime-stable external store. Typing, flushing, preparing, replacing, clearing, restoring, and remotely synchronizing a prompt must not place the prompt text or reset counters in `ActionPopupContent` or its controller React state.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis job must land before the major action-popup ownership and subscription refactor.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current architecture\\r\\n\\r\\nPrompt ownership is duplicated:\\r\\n\\r\\n- `useActionPopupController` stores prompt value, preparation status, and reset token in React state.\\r\\n- `ActionPopupContent` creates a new `ActionPromptDraft` whenever the controller prompt or reset token changes.\\r\\n- `ActionPromptDraft` buffers live editor values and supports a narrow bottom-row subscription.\\r\\n- `ActionExecutionService` separately stores prompt values, revisions, pending bridge writes, and remote prompt sessions.\\r\\n\\r\\nOrdinary typing already stays out of root React state because `MarkdownEditor.onLiveChange` writes to `ActionPromptDraft`. Editor flush still calls `setPromptState`, and external preparation/replacement/clear operations update root state and replace the draft object. Those paths rerender the complete popup.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required ownership\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate one prompt-draft service that owns stable draft stores keyed by the action context and, when applicable, the active agent session. The service is justified because it owns state, draft lifecycle, asynchronous bridge synchronization, revisions, and pending writes.\\r\\n\\r\\nMove the current prompt-draft map and remote prompt-session behavior out of `ActionExecutionService`. The renamed run/session service planned by the later popup refactor must not retain prompt text ownership.\\r\\n\\r\\nEach stable draft store exposes, at minimum:\\r\\n\\r\\n- current Markdown value;\\r\\n- preparation state: `loading`, `ready`, or `failed`;\\r\\n- a narrow subscription contract suitable for `useSyncExternalStore`;\\r\\n- local edit without React parent state;\\r\\n- external replacement that notifies the editor to call `setMarkdown` once;\\r\\n- clear, flush/synchronize, send, and current-value reads;\\r\\n- revision protection for superseded asynchronous preparation and remote writes.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not add arbitrary retention limits or silent eviction. Draft removal must follow explicit lifecycle events such as successful send, deliberate clear, action removal, or project teardown. A popup unmount does not discard an unsent draft.\\r\\n\\r\\n\\n===== J_023_use_one_agent_conversation_model.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-023\\r\\ninternalId: 1244ac27-293a-4a5f-b478-0890ecc3fea6\\r\\ntitle: use one agent conversation model while growing and persisted\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n  - app/src/data/action_run_types.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/data/data_types.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/services/actions/action_execution_service.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/use_action_popup_controller.ts\\r\\n  - desktop/src/actions/action/action_execution.js\\r\\n  - desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_runner_service.js\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n  checkLinting: true\\r\\n  requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: 5b39ff1e-4bbc-4d50-b527-36e1d1faa6f5\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nFollow J-020 by removing the remaining `LiveAgentTurn` model. A growing conversation and a persisted conversation are the same `AgentConversation`; persistence is only a lifecycle state.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current problem\\r\\n\\r\\nJ-020 unified conversation content into `entries`, but renderer run state still stores `LiveAgentTurn`. `useActionPopupController` converts that object into a new `AgentConversation` during rendering. This duplicates models, metadata, and ownership.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required change\\r\\n\\r\\n- Remove `LiveAgentTurn` and `liveAgentConversation`.\\r\\n- Store `AgentConversation | null` directly in run state.\\r\\n- Make the agent-start event provide the complete canonical conversation snapshot, including identity, metadata, path, status, and initial entries.\\r\\n- Apply later message/event updates immutably to that conversation's `entries` without changing entry order.\\r\\n- Apply status and completion metadata to the same model.\\r\\n- Persist and reload the same `AgentConversation` shape.\\r\\n- Continuation starts from the canonical source conversation and adds new entries without a renderer-side merge.\\r\\n- Do not add live/persisted adapters, compatibility shapes, or duplicated fields.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] `LiveAgentTurn` and `liveAgentConversation` no longer exist.\\r\\n- [ ] Growing, completed, persisted, loaded, and continued conversations all use `AgentConversation`.\\r\\n- [ ] Run state exposes the canonical conversation directly.\\r\\n- [ ] Popup rendering performs no conversation-shape conversion or history merge.\\r\\n- [ ] Entry identity and order remain stable during streamed updates.\\r\\n- [ ] App and desktop lint and tests pass.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Dependency\\r\\n\\r\\nJ-020 must be implemented first.\\r\\n\\n===== J_024_replace_execution_state_with_scoped_action_runs.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-024\\r\\ninternalId: 1975a005-f0bb-432f-8ecb-bc85a27819d2\\r\\ntitle: replace global execution state with scoped action runs\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n  - app/src/data/action_run_types.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/data/electron_action_bridge.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/components/hooks/use_action_executions.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/services/actions/action_execution_service.ts\\r\\n  - desktop/src/actions/action/action_execution.js\\r\\n  - desktop/src/actions/action/action_runner_service.js\\r\\n  - desktop/src/shell/local_bridge_dispatch.js\\r\\n  - desktop/src/shell/preload.js\\r\\n  - shared/card_activity.mjs\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n  checkLinting: true\\r\\n  requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: 1244ac27-293a-4a5f-b478-0890ecc3fea6\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nReplace execution terminology and the global renderer snapshot with action-run terminology, a routing registry, and stable scoped run stores.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Terminology\\r\\n\\r\\n- `runId`, not `executionId`.\\r\\n- `ActionRun`, not `LiveActionExecution` or action execution.\\r\\n- `ActionRunRegistry`, not `ActionExecutionService`.\\r\\n- `ActionRunStore`: stable state owner for one run.\\r\\n- `runs`, not `executions`.\\r\\n- `ConversationEntry` remains reserved for items inside an agent conversation.\\r\\n\\r\\nRename the contract consistently across Electron, bridge messages, renderer services, hooks, persisted action records, errors, and tests. Process execution may keep that term only where it refers to an operating-system process.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Registry shape\\r\\n\\r\\n`ActionRunRegistry` keeps one renderer-wide bridge subscription and a routing map from `runId` to stable `ActionRunStore`. The map is an internal index, not a React snapshot.\\r\\n\\r\\nEach `ActionRunStore` owns one run's status, logs, root action, active chained action, context, conversation, approvals, and question. Unrelated run changes must preserve selected store snapshots and must not render their consumers.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Persistence and lifecycle\\r\\n\\r\\n\\n===== J_025_move_action_popup_state_to_leaf_owners.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor:\\r\\nid: J-025\\r\\ninternalId: 96705093-a302-409d-b626-fe3e16fd28e2\\r\\ntitle: move action popup state and subscriptions to leaf owners\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner:\\r\\naffects:\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/action_popup.tsx\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/action_popup_content.tsx\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/use_action_popup_controller.ts\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/action_selector.tsx\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/action_conversation_chat.tsx\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/action_log_error_display.tsx\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/action_agent_approval.tsx\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/action_agent_question.tsx\\r\\n  - app/src/components/actions/action_popup_bottom_row.tsx\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\n  checkLinting: true\\r\\n  requireTests: true\\r\\nafter: 1975a005-f0bb-432f-8ecb-bc85a27819d2\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Goal\\r\\n\\r\\nMake popup roots own layout and selection only. The processes appear as **Git for Windows** in Task Manager and accumulate across runs.\\r\\n\\r\\nObserved processes were executing normally short-lived commands such as `config`, `rev-parse`, `remote -v`, and `status --porcelain`. They remained alive after their immediate parent processes had exited.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current implementation\\r\\n\\r\\nMDÂ² starts agents through `AgentRunnerService`. When an agent closes normally, `handleClose` queries the current Windows process tree and terminates descendants of the agent PID. Cancellation terminates the process tree with `taskkill /t /f`.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis cleanup cannot discover a surviving Git process after an intermediate parent has already exited: the current process snapshot no longer contains a complete chain from the agent PID to that Git process. The observed Git processes had dead immediate parents, matching this failure mode.\\r\\n\\r\\nMDÂ² also invokes Git directly through `git_commands.js`. These calls have no timeout or cancellation handling, so an independently hung app-owned Git command can block its caller indefinitely.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Investigation plan\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Reproduce with MDÂ² open but no agent run, then while starting and completing or cancelling an agent run.\\r\\n2. Record every spawned Git PID, command, working directory, parent PID, agent run ID, and lifecycle event.\\r\\n3. Run an affected command under a bounded external timeout with Git tracing enabled to locate the blocking operation.\\r\\n4. Check repository state, Git configuration, filesystem monitoring, antivirus or file locks, and agent shutdown ordering.\\r\\n5. Confirm whether Git descendants become disconnected before `AgentRunnerService.handleClose` takes its process snapshot.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required change\\r\\n\\r\\n- Track enough process ownership during an agent run to terminate surviving descendants even when intermediate processes exit before final cleanup.\\r\\n- Clean up owned descendants when an agent completes, fails, is cancelled, or crashes.\\r\\n- Do not terminate unrelated Git processes or Git work started outside the corresponding MDÂ² agent run.\\r\\n- Add a bounded timeout and process cleanup to direct Git execution in `git_commands.js`.\\r\\n- Include the command, working directory, elapsed time, and owning run or app operation in timeout diagnostics.\\r\\n- Deduplicate or serialize repeated read-only metadata probes only if tracing confirms they contribute to the accumulation.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Failure modes and compatibility\\r\\n\\r\\n- PID reuse must not allow cleanup to target a process that MDÂ² did not start.\\r\\n- Cleanup must cover shell and helper-process chains used by Git for Windows on Windows.\\r\\n- Long-running network Git operations need an explicit, suitable timeout rather than the same threshold as local metadata commands.\\r\\n- Existing agent cancellation, command actions, commits, worktree operations, push, pull, and fetch behavior must remain unchanged apart from bounded failure and cleanup.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- [ ] Completing, failing, cancelling, or crashing an agent run leaves no Git processes owned by that run.\\r\\n- [ ] Repeated agent runs do not accumulate Git for Windows processes.\\r\\n\\n===== B_85_add_the_reference_to_a_chatlog_to_a_card_as_soon_as_possible.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: B_85\\r\\ninternalId: 56dd54b0-9554-4545-85d4-bb45efef4d6e\\r\\ntitle: add the reference to a chatlog to a card as soon as possible\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\n  - Failed and declined reasoning already use the error presentation.\\r\\n\\r\\n## implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Filter conversation feed activities in `ActionConversationChat`: omit only events where `type === 'reasoning'` and `status === 'completed'`.\\r\\n- Keep in-progress, failed, declined and unknown-status reasoning visible.\\r\\n- Keep completed reasoning events in conversation data and persisted history; this is a presentation-only change.\\r\\n- Update chat tests for live completion, reopened conversations, failed/declined reasoning and unaffected non-reasoning activities.\\r\\n\\r\\n## acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- In-progress reasoning is visible.\\r\\n- A reasoning block disappears when its status becomes `completed`, including after reopening a conversation.\\r\\n- Failed and declined reasoning remains visible with its error state and content.\\r\\n- Completed non-reasoning activities remain visible.\\r\\n\\n===== F_94_no_prefill_prompt_running_conv.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_94\\r\\ninternalId: d4afff38-5581-42f4-a8f3-8ded807ab27a\\r\\ntitle: no prefill prompt running conv\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 3ffa4da3-1e0f-4930-ad38-6bf247b13c52\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen an agent is waiting for a response, but the action popup was closed or on the wrong 'action', then when the user clicks on the action to view the conversation and answer, the input box is prefilled again with the action's prompt. this is annoying cause it needs to be removed.\\r\\n\\r\\nso, when activating an action that has a running conversation, don't prefill the input\\r\\n\\r\\n# Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`useActionPopupController` prepares an action's stored prompt for a new conversation. When popup opens on another action, or reopens while execution state is being restored, that prepared prompt can remain in `promptState` when user selects action with a `queued`, `running`, or `waitingForInput` conversation.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Give active execution its own prompt identity, including before active-child metadata arrives.\\r\\n- When active action is selected, seed editor only from its shared user-entered draft; otherwise show empty input.\\r\\n- Invalidate pending prompt preparation and bump `promptResetToken` when action becomes active.\\r\\n- Keep stored-prompt prefill for idle actions starting new conversations. Keep command actions unchanged.\\r\\n\\r\\n# Acceptance criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n- Selecting or reopening action with active conversation does not prefill its stored action prompt.\\r\\n- Existing user-entered draft for active conversation is restored.\\r\\n- Late prompt-preparation result cannot overwrite active conversation input.\\r\\n- Idle agent actions still prefill stored prompt.\\r\\n- Controller and popup tests cover action switching, popup reopen, draft restore, and preparation race.\\r\\n\\n===== F_95_integrate_into_project_should_track_commit.md =====\\r\\n---\\r\\nauthor: \\r\\nid: F_95\\r\\ninternalId: e5b95f2c-cd0c-4623-8e12-d0c497447e71\\r\\ntitle: integrate into project should track commit\\r\\nstatus: ready\\r\\nowner: \\r\\naffects:\\r\\nagents:\\r\\n  - design/activity/card__e5b95f2c-cd0c-4623-8e12-d0c497447e71.json#conversation=agent-4e6f97b9-647e-49fc-93f7-cf09e5eff1aa\\r\\npolicy:\\r\\nafter: 9ef42f8e-d6f7-4514-8e4a-5555318c4b51\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## Current state\\r\\n\\r\\n`WorktreeSelector` integrates an assigned card through `WorktreeService` and the Electron worktree service. The backend checkpoints primary-worktree changes, rebases the card branch when behind, then fast-forwards the project branch. The operation returns no commit metadata.\\r\\n\\r\\nCard commit history reads tracked `<projectFolder>/activity/card__<cardInternalId>.json` files. Only action executions add commit references, so commits integrated from the selector are absent unless an action already recorded them.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Implementation details\\r\\n\\r\\n- Add a card-specific integration request containing `cardInternalId` and `projectFolder`; project-level worktree integration remains untracked.\\r\\n- After any rebase, squash the card branch's complete change onto the project branch and create one integration commit.
